{"world_model":"W6 model after E050. Time ≈ 0.1 s fixed + steps × per-step cost. Per-step cost = pixel-proportional compute + a bandwidth-bound part (BN/GELU/pointwise, ~27% of a 32 px step). Tip E049: 5.198 s, 0.7535 on seeds 0–2. The population mean is ~0.752, only ~0.2 pp over the bar. E050 re-read the same recipe at 0.7552 and 5.206 s, so I treat that as noise.

Mechanisms and support:
1. Accuracy rises slowly with optimizer steps, about 1.5–2.5 s/pp. Pure step, epoch and sample cuts trade at dial-like rates (E020, E031, E040, E041, E037, E045, E048).
2. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
3. Late backward truncation saves more than its MAC share. Frozen blocks also skip BN/GELU backward, optimizer updates and Lookahead traffic. Support: E028, E034, E036, E046, E049. Late freezes are roughly neutral. Early ones are not (E037's cliff). This is the one lever that keeps working. Each added freeze yields about 0.1–0.2 s.
4. Averaging, LS, warm-up, Lookahead-interval, BN-recalibration and batch-split tweaks are null or negative (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, E045). The recipe is near a local optimum, so I shade non-systems changes by -0.1 pp.
5. Math-identical systems work is worth 1–2% each (E035). Only ~2.5% of GPU time is outside the step graphs (E047). E050 is a pure diagnostic.
6. wd ×0.5 helped ~0.2 pp (E016). Muon's gain is confounded.
7. Elementwise and activation work is bytes-bound, so ReLU should save 1–3%. Removing a full-resolution tensor (I080) should save more, but it changes the architecture and may cost accuracy.
8. Build-to-build kernel reselection moves 3-seed accuracy by up to ~0.3 pp. This is the main decision noise. Time noise is ±0.04 s.

Misses: truncation and selection savings beat my estimates (E037, E041, E046, E048). Accuracy swung ±0.3 pp on identical code. Lesson: use wide accuracy ranges. Treat differences below 0.3 pp on 3 seeds as noise. Expect freezes and step cuts to save slightly more than linear.

W6 model after E050. Time ≈ 0.1 s fixed + steps × per-step cost. Per-step cost = pixel-proportional compute + a bandwidth-bound part (BN/GELU/pointwise, ~27% of a 32 px step). Tip E049: 5.198 s, 0.7535 on seeds 0–2. The population mean is ~0.752, only ~0.2 pp over the bar. E050 re-read the same recipe at 0.7552 and 5.206 s, so I treat that as noise.

Mechanisms and support:
1. Accuracy rises slowly with optimizer steps, about 1.5–2.5 s/pp. Pure step, epoch and sample cuts trade at dial-like rates (E020, E031, E040, E041, E037, E045, E048).
2. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
3. Late backward truncation saves more than its MAC share. Frozen blocks also skip BN/GELU backward, optimizer updates and Lookahead traffic. Support: E028, E034, E036, E046, E049. Late freezes are roughly neutral. Early ones are not (E037's cliff). This is the one lever that keeps working. Each added freeze yields about 0.1–0.2 s.
4. Averaging, LS, warm-up, Lookahead-interval, BN-recalibration and batch-split tweaks are null or negative (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, E045). The recipe is near a local optimum, so I shade non-systems changes by -0.1 pp.
5. Math-identical systems work is worth 1–2% each (E035). Only ~2.5% of GPU time is outside the step graphs (E047). E050 is a pure diagnostic.
6. wd ×0.5 helped ~0.2 pp (E016). Muon's gain is confounded.
7. Elementwise and activation work is bytes-bound, so ReLU should save 1–3%. Removing a full-resolution tensor (I080) should save more, but it changes the architecture and may cost accuracy.
8. Build-to-build kernel reselection moves 3-seed accuracy by up to ~0.3 pp. This is the main decision noise. Time noise is ±0.04 s.

Misses: truncation and selection savings beat my estimates (E037, E041, E046, E048). Accuracy swung ±0.3 pp on identical code. Lesson: use wide accuracy ranges. Treat differences below 0.3 pp on 3 seeds as noise. Expect freezes and step cuts to save slightly more than linear.

Unsure: the true tip mean (0.752 ± 0.1), selection bias, transfer to the PCIe judge, how far the group-2 freeze can extend, and whether stride-2 conv can replace conv+pool without an accuracy loss.

forecasts.reason: ReLU saves a little bytes-bound time and may cost a little accuracy; both effects are inside noise.
Stride-2 conv drops the 31x31 tensor and its pool, saving time. It also removes the max-pool nonlinearity, which could cost accuracy.
Selection plus a top-up is roughly neutral against the dial; the net step count barely changes.
A longer group-2 freeze saves about 0.08 s, but an annealed freeze from 70% is near the E037 cliff.

cruxes: Is the tip's true population mean (~0.752) really above the 0.75 official bar? If it is lower, every time cut is unsafe and the next step is to buy margin.
Does the stem's 31x31 conv+pool block cost much more than its FLOP share, and can stride-2 replace it without an accuracy loss (I080)?
How far can the late-freeze cascade extend: is the group-2 freeze at 85% still neutral, or does it hit an E037-style cliff?
